description: Agent Construction: submit a building permit as issued with the project record: the permit with its issuer, permit number, project address, holder, each item of work it covers as printed, the day issued and its expiry; the project record with the permit number, the project address, the contractor, each item of work the project calls for, the permit expiry the record shows and the days work starts and is scheduled to end. The signed report gives the permit and the project record, the permit number and the address on each side read as matching or differing, the project work matched to the permitted scope with the items uncovered and the permitted items unused, and the expiry printed against the expiry recorded and the work schedule, and counts them, and names a mismatched permit: a permit number or project address unlike the project record, an item of project work the permitted scope does not cover, a recorded expiry later than the permit prints, and work scheduled to end after the permit expires; then a permitted item the project record leaves out, another holder than the recorded contractor, an earlier recorded expiry and work scheduled to start before the permit was issued, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No permit number or address on either side, no work listed on either side, or no expiry on the permit leaves the permit unverified. Permit numbers match by their letters and digits, addresses with their street abbreviations spelled out, and scope items by their words. This check reports whether the permit matches the project record; it makes no building-code compliance determination. Beside it, wever_certification-evidence-check reads certification, compliance or license claims against the evidence offered for them, and wever_realty-disclosure-check reads a seller disclosure against the property records, while the permit check reads a building permit’s number, address, scope and expiry against the project it was issued for. Verdict build_permit_mismatched, build_permit_partial, build_permit_unverified or build_permit_matched. POST /api/build-permit-check. Reads the construction paperwork supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only, with no structural, engineering or safety judgment, building-code compliance determination, valuation of work performed or legal advice on contracts, liens or permits, and the paperwork stays in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Construction reads supplied construction paperwork for consistency between documents: a building permit, a contractor license record, a bid, a construction contract, a change order, a lien waiver, a completion certificate or punch list record, and a payment application. Beside it, wever_workorder-create and the other wever_workorder tools and wever_agent-work-order-exchange are the action layer that creates, funds, delivers and releases work orders, while this family moves nothing and executes nothing and only reads paperwork; wever_agent-escrow-lite holds and releases escrowed funds, and escrow stays there; and the Agent Real Estate checks such as wever_realty-title-check read property records by parcel and address, not a project’s construction paperwork. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-construction-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-construction/.
